# Actual zero-forest roof patches and an exact mass exchange

An actual homothetic zero-slack forest decomposes into integer-complete affine roof patches: every terminal basin lies in the minimal radius-graph face of its terminal root, and the continuous centroids are affine on each entire patch. This uses actual convex-fiber compatibility, beyond the abstract coefficient conditions.

Independent relative-Helly bounds on those patches do not automatically give the desired aggregate budget. Section 4 gives an actual rational eight-fiber counterexample to that precise inference. Section 5 then proves a stronger weighted-depth bound for the **entire eight-node incidence pattern**, using a shared ray of sources and an exact two-case mass exchange. This covers every homothetic radius choice allowed by the forest, not only the previously archived one-parameter family. No patch-gluing assertion for arbitrary forests is made.

## 1. The actual radius graph and its upper faces

Let `C` be compact convex, with finite positive `d`-volume integer-fiber set `P`, `d>=1`. Assume all positive fibers are translates and positive homothetic copies of a common full-dimensional convex body:

    K_p=a_p+r_p K,       r_p>0,       centroid(K)=0.

Thus `a_p` is the true fiber centroid. Work in the affine base span of `P`, of dimension `m<=n`. Let

    G_p=(p,r_p),          Qhat=conv{G_p:p in P}.         (1)

Actual convexity and Brunn--Minkowski give, for every anchored convex combination with integer target,

    p=sum lambda_i p_i  ==>  r_p>=sum lambda_i r_pi.    (2)

Every `G_p` is therefore on the upper boundary of `Qhat`: no convex combination of the lifted points with base `p` has greater height. More precisely, each `G_p` belongs to a face exposed by a functional whose height coefficient is positive. Here is a finite justification which includes boundary bases. The linear program maximizing `sum lambda_i r_pi` subject to `lambda_i>=0`, `sum lambda_i=1`, and `sum lambda_i p_i=p` is feasible and has attained value `r_p` by (2). Its dual has an attained affine majorant `ell` with

    ell(q)>=r_q for all q in P,       ell(p)=r_p.

Both primal and dual are feasible and bounded; this is ordinary finite linear-programming duality. Hence the plane `r=ell(z)` supports the upper side of `Qhat` at `G_p`.

If `r_p` is affine on all bases, the radius graph is an affine copy of `P` and has dimension `m`; its minimal faces may include the whole graph. Otherwise `Qhat` has dimension `m+1`, and the minimal face `F_p` containing `G_p` is a proper upper face of dimension at most `m`. In both cases projection onto the base is injective and affine on every such face. The radius graph must not be confused with the translated centroid graph: affine radii alone do not assert that all centroid translations are globally affine.

## 2. Face filtration along the forest

Suppose the designated parity-root forest terminates and every edge is an exact Minkowski equality:

    F(p)=(p+v_c)/2,
    K_F(p)=(K_p+K_vc)/2.                              (3)

Here `v_c` is the volume-maximal root of the parity class of `p`; for the face-filtration conclusion only termination and the exact set identity are needed. Homothety gives

    G_F(p)=(G_p+G_vc)/2,
    a_F(p)=(a_p+a_vc)/2.                              (4)

If a face of a convex polytope contains the midpoint of two of its points, it contains both endpoints: apply an exposing functional and equality in its two upper bounds. In particular,

    F_p subset F_F(p),        F_vc subset F_F(p).        (5)

Along a terminating path, minimal faces only enlarge. Thus every point in the terminal basin of root `v_j` belongs to `F_vj`. Every partner root used anywhere on that path also belongs to `F_vj`.

The faces `F_vj` therefore cover the entire radius graph. Retain only the inclusion-maximal distinct root faces; their union still covers the graph. Different maximal patches can overlap on proper boundary faces. Terminal basins themselves are disjoint, but the complete patches generally are not.

## 3. Integer completion and affine centroids on an entire root patch

Fix a terminal root `v`, its minimal face `F=F_v`, and the projected polytope `Q_F=pi(F)`. Let `P_F={p in P:G_p in F}`. Choose an affine upper majorant `ell` exposing an upper face containing `F`. For any integer `z in Q_F`, write its lift in `F` as a convex combination of graph points of `F`. Equation (2) and the majorant bound imply

    r_z>=ell(z),       r_z<=ell(z).

The first inequality also proves positive volume at `z`, so `z in P`. The lifted point `(z,r_z)` is the point of `F` with base `z`. Therefore

    P_F=Q_F intersect Z^n,       r_p=ell(p) on P_F.     (6)

This uses the actual common intersection with the base lattice. It does not replace the terminal basin by an arbitrary subset of its affine span.

The root `v` is in the relative interior of `Q_F`, because `G_v` is in the relative interior of its minimal face and projection is an affine isomorphism there. We next show that the **actual centroid map** is affine on all of `P_F`.

For every convex representation `z=sum lambda_i p_i` within `P_F` whose target `z` is integer, equality of the affine radii in (6) implies

    sum lambda_i K_pi
       =(sum lambda_i a_pi)+r_z K subset K_z=a_z+r_z K.

The two full-dimensional convex bodies have equal volume. Proper inclusion of compact convex bodies with positive full volume would create a positive-volume missing cone, so inclusion is equality. Their centroids are equal:

    a_z=sum lambda_i a_pi.                            (7)

To convert all these anchored identities into one affine map, choose a strictly positive convex representation of `v` using **every** point of the finite set `P_F`. Such a representation exists because `v` is relatively interior: for each point `p`, a sufficiently small positive coefficient at `p` leaves a residual point in `Q_F`; average these finitely many representations. If `(alpha_p)` is any affine dependence, `sum alpha_p=0` and `sum alpha_p p=0`, both sufficiently small positive and negative perturbations of the strictly positive coefficients still represent `v`. Apply (7) to both and subtract. It follows that `sum alpha_p a_p=0`. Thus there is an affine map `A_F` on `aff Q_F` satisfying

    a_p=A_F(p) for all p in P_F.                       (8)

Consequently the entire centroid patch is an affine image of the lattice-convex set `P_F`. Its weighted source-center bound can use its actual relative Helly number `h(P_F)`, or the weaker `2^(dim Q_F)`. This establishes the decomposition, including translated homothetic fibers, without presuming that separate patch bounds can be added.

## 4. An actual counterexample to independent patch-mass allocation

Use the eight bases from `candidate 588eabf65d9a1440`, indexed as follows:

    0=(-1,-2), 1=(-1,-1), 2=(-1,0), 3=(0,0),
    4=(0,1),   5=(0,2),   6=(1,2),  7=(2,3).

Their convex hull `Q` has exactly those integer points and is described by

    -2 z1+z2<=2,  -z1<=1,  -z1+2 z2<=4,
    5 z1-3 z2<=1.                                    (9)

Take one continuous coordinate and define

    r(z)=min{1+z2/4, 17/25-(8/25)z1},
    C={(z,x):z in Q, 0<=x<=r(z)}.                    (10)

Both displayed affine functions are positive at every vertex where they define the minimum; the minimum radius on `Q` is `1/25`. The hypograph description makes `C` a full-dimensional compact convex polytope. Its eight fiber lengths, in units `1/100`, are

    (50,75,100,68,68,68,36,4),       total T=469.       (11)

The parity roots remain `2,1,3,4`. Root 3 ties root-class point 5 in radius, but is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm point of that tied class. All other nontrivial comparisons are strict. The nonroot edges are

    0->1 with partner 2,     5->4 with partner 3,
    6->4 with partner 2,     7->6 with partner 4.       (12)

They have the exact radius identities

    50+100=2*75,   68+68=2*68,
    36+100=2*68,   4+68=2*36.

For intervals `[0,r]` these are the actual set equalities in (3).

The minimal upper faces of the four roots, as index sets, are

    F_1={0,1,2},     F_2={2},     F_3={3},
    F_4={2,3,4,5,6,7}.                               (13)

Thus the maximal patches are the line `E={0,1,2}` and the plane `F={2,3,4,5,6,7}`, intersecting only at point 2. They have exact relative Helly numbers

    h(P_E)=2,       h(P_F)=3.                         (14)

For (14), the line has three consecutive integer points and ordinary interval Helly number two. The planar set is the lattice-convex quadrilateral with vertex indices `(2,3,7,5)` and the additional points 4 and 6. A three-point empty triangle, for example indices `{2,3,4}`, gives a three-set witness. To exclude a four-set witness, the only convex-position four-subsets are `{2,3,5,6}` and `{2,3,5,7}`. For the first, point 4 lies in every deletion hull through the two disjoint pairs `(2,6)` and `(3,5)`. For the second, point 4 again lies in every deletion hull: `p_4=(2/3)p_2+(1/3)p_7=(1/2)p_3+(1/2)p_5`. Equivalently one may use the finite-set deletion-kernel characterization together with planar Helly at most four. The independent certificate `candidate f1f97e5764053b3f` and its standard-library verifier enumerate the six-point set exactly; no floating-point convex hull is used.

In the units of (11),

    W(E)=225,       W(F)=344,       W(E intersect F)=100.

The overlap is counted exactly, so `T=225+344-100=469`. Nevertheless,

    max{W(E)/h(P_E),W(F)/h(P_F)}
         =344/3 <469/4=T/4.                          (15)

Therefore independent relative-Helly patch-mass bounds do **not** imply the desired four-root budget, even with actual convexity, all integer completions, exact overlap mass, and the prescribed volume-maximal forest. Equation (15) is not a counterexample to weighted depth at actual graph points.

## 5. A four-budget mass exchange for the entire eight-node pattern

Here is the extra incidence that independent patch bounds miss. Work with the **centroid graph** of any actual homothetic family having the eight-node forest pattern (12), in any continuous dimension `d>=1`. The common shape and translation of the fibers may vary between different families; within a given family they obey (1). Let `w_i=|K_i|`.

The root-maximality comparisons and the midpoint radius identities imply

    w_0<=w_2,      w_5<=w_3,
    w_6,w_7<=w_4<=w_2.                               (16)

Indeed, the first two and `w_7<=w_4` are direct parity-root comparisons. The last edge gives `r_6=(r_7+r_4)/2<=r_4`; the preceding edge gives `r_2=2r_4-r_6>=r_4`. Positive powers preserve their order.

Use the five disjoint mass blocks

    A=w_3,     G=w_2,     L=w_0+w_1,
    B=w_4+w_5,     C=w_6+w_7.

Their total is the full source mass

    T=A+G+L+B+C.                                     (17)

The graph points at 3 and 2 have atomic containing-cap depth at least `A` and `G`. Point 1 is the midpoint of graph points 0 and 2. By (16), every containing closed halfspace has mass at least

    w_1+min(w_0,w_2)=L.                              (18)

At graph point 4 there are two distinct line directions. Points 3 and 5 are an opposite pair about 4. On the other line,

    G_6-G_4=G_4-G_2,
    G_7-G_4=2(G_4-G_2),                              (19)

where `G_i=(p_i,a_i)` now denotes the full centroid graph. Thus points 6 and 7 are on the **same** ray opposite point 2. Any closed halfspace containing 4 contains either point 2 or both points 6 and 7; if its boundary contains the line, all three are included. Combining the two disjoint line groups with point 4 gives the exact guaranteed mass

    w_4+min(w_3,w_5)+min(w_2,w_6+w_7)
       = B+min(G,C).                                (20)

Let

    D=max{A,G,L,B+min(G,C)}.                          (21)

Equations (18)--(20) give an actual deterministic graph point with depth at least `D`. The decisive remaining inequality is

    C<=2w_4<=w_4+w_2<=B+G.                           (22)

It follows directly from (16), and retains the shared point-2 mass rather than subtracting an abstract overlap cost. There are two cases:

* If `C<=G`, then `D>=B+C`, and (17) is the sum of the four blocks `A,G,L,B+C`, each at most `D`.
* If `C>G`, then `D>=B+G`; now use the four blocks `A,L,B+G,C`. Equation (22) ensures the last block is also at most `D`.

In both cases,

    T<=4D.                                          (23)

This proves weighted graph depth at least `T/4` for **every** homothetic zero-slack family on this incidence pattern, including all its allowed nonuniform radius choices. In fact the finite graph argument needs only the midpoint/ray identities and the weight inequalities (16), not full convexity once those have been supplied.

Ordinary Grunbaum at every counted fiber centroid upgrades (23) to an original mixed containing-cap mass at least `Gamma_d T/4`. Every cap is ambient and closed; zero continuous-normal restrictions only increase the contribution from a counted fiber.

For the rational counterexample (11), the scores are

    A=68, G=100, L=125, B=136, C=40,
    D=max(68,100,125,176)=176>469/4.

Thus that actual family simultaneously certifies failure of the separate patch-mass inference and success of the stronger incidence-based mass exchange. No assertion that these lower scores equal the exact maximal graph depth is needed.

## 6. Scope and dependencies

The general conclusions are the exact face filtration, integer completion, and affine-centroid patch description in Sections 1--3. The positive aggregate theorem (23) is restricted to the displayed eight-node incidence pattern. The obstruction (15) rules out one natural independent-patch allocation, not every possible overlap-sensitive argument.

The old base polygon and forest are independently certified in `candidate 588eabf65d9a1440`. The exact face and relative-Helly computation is independently proved in `candidate f1f97e5764053b3f`, with verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_eight_base_upper_faces_and_patch_budget.py`. The new radius profile, edge orders, grouped-ray incidences, and mass arithmetic are also checked by `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_actual_zero_forest_roof_patch_exchange.py`. The proofs use actual source convexity, Brunn--Minkowski, finite linear-programming duality, and ordinary relative Helly/Doignon; they do not use OC as an assumption.

A subsequent exact actual-family obstruction is saved in `candidate 90f577d65c14ec9f`: its nine-node zero-slack forest has maximum weighted centroid-graph depth `10/43<1/4`. Thus the face decomposition cannot imply a universal graph-only charging theorem. The eight-node exchange theorem above remains valid, and the new counterexample separately has sufficient original continuous-volume depth.
